title: When the Whole Service Fails
intro: A fridge repair turned into 46 days of looping chatbots, cancelled appointments and broken escalation.

learn.title: 46 days, by the numbers
learn.text:
• ~**8.5 hours** on the phone with customer service
• ~**64 trips** up and down the basement stairs with bags of ice packs
• ~**$600** of groceries thrown away
• ~**$1,000** in takeaway and unexpected restaurant meals
• **4** technician visits
• **3** Post-its of 1-800 numbers, extensions and dead-end routes

Outcome: “I will never shop at Sears again.”

try.q: What is the outcome that matters commercially?
options: The cost of the repair visits
The time spent on the phone
try.explain: Everything else is recoverable; that isn't.

learn.title: The failure wasn't the interface
learn.text:
No screen caused this. The service **couldn't handle an exception** — an out-of-stock part, a delay, a customer who had already called five times.

Chatbots looped. Escalation paths dead-ended. Each call started from zero.

As UX professionals, we talk a lot about empathy. **Empathy without the infrastructure to support it means nothing.**

try.q: What did the service fail to handle?
try.explain: Delays, missing parts and repeat contacts are normal, not edge cases.

left.label: Designed for
items: The repair that goes to plan

right.label: What actually happens
items: The fifth call about the same issue

learn.title: What this means for design
learn.text:
**Design for exceptions:** out-of-stock parts, delays, rescheduling, a customer who has already called five times.

**Give people a path to a human who can actually act** — not one who can only read the same script.

Service blueprints expose exactly these failure points, which is why they beat an imagined journey map.

try.q: Which artefact would have exposed these failure points?
try.explain: It documents backstage systems, owners and hand-offs — where this broke.

test.q: How long did the ordeal last?
test.explain: From the day the fridge stopped cooling.

test.q: Why does Calabro call this a UX story?
options: The experience is the whole service, not the screen
The website was hard to navigate
test.explain: He usually writes about research; this was deliberate.

test.q: What does empathy need to be worth anything?
options: Infrastructure that supports acting on it
test.explain: Otherwise it's a sentiment with no mechanism.

test.q: What should an escalation path lead to?
test.explain: A human reading the same script is still a dead end.

test.q: Which of these is an exception a service should design for?
options: A customer calling for the fifth time
test.explain: The repeat contact is where the experience is decided.
